contests.name: Constitutional Amendment A
contests.description: Constitutional Amendment A would replace the requirement that proposed constitutional amendments be published in newspapers in every county with a publication method set by state law. Under the implementing statute, the full text of proposed amendments and other legislative ballot questions would be posted on the Utah Public Notice Website and the Lieutenant Governor's website for 60 days before the general election. The amendment would take effect January 1, 2027, if approved.

contests.name: Constitutional Amendment B
contests.description: Constitutional Amendment B would require statewide citizen-proposed laws that increase taxes compared to existing law to be approved by at least 60% of voters rather than a simple majority. It would cover initiatives that create a new tax, expand an existing tax, increase a tax rate, or change a property tax rate so that it decreases less than current law would. Other statewide initiatives would continue to require a simple majority, and the change would apply to initiatives voted on after November 1, 2026.
